BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph S. 2621 OPINION AUG 21 2024 MR. CESAR V. BERGULA Brgy. District II, Babatngon, Leyte C/o Atty. Sam Dominic T. Lagunzad T. Claudio St., Brgy. 8, Tacloban City Dear Mr. Bergula: This has reference to the request for legal opinion with regard to your claim for back wages as a former sangguniang bayan member who has been acquitted for violation of RA 9165. The DILG Regional Office has previously answered your inquiry and has now elevated the matter to our level for further guidance. You maintain the following facts and circumstances: You are the former municipal councilor of the Municipality of Babatngon, Leyte, and was detained for a period of three (3) years from 3 July 2020 until 8 August 2023 when the Regional Trial Court acquitted you of the offense charged. The concerned local government unit denied you of your monetary claim due to your absence from sanggunian sessions and failure to render public service during said period. You stress that you were legally prevented from attending the sessions due to your detention. It is worth mentioning that the dispositive portion of the judgement in your case of People of the Philippines vs. Cesar Bergula y Viadorl, for violations of Sections 5 & 11, Article II of RA 9165, provides: WHEREFORE, foregoing considered, judgment is hereby rendered ACQUITTING the accused CESAR BEGULAR y VIADOR of the two (2) charges against him for Violation of Sections 5 & II, Article II of RA 9165, due to reasonable doubt of his guilt. xxx Moreover, in the body of the aforementioned decision, the court found that the prosecution failed to (1) prove all elements of violation of Sections 5 & 11 of RA 9165, as the buy bust operation did not pass the objective test; (2) overcome accused's presumption of innocence; (3) offer any explanation for the failure to strictly comply with Sec. 21 , Article II of RA 9165 as amended; and (4) prove the corpus delicti of the crime with moral certainty in view of the unexplained lapses in procedures For these reasons, the court was constrained to acquit you from the charges filed against you. Notwithstanding the matters you have raised in your letter, we affirm the findings of the regional office and maintain that it has sufficiently addressed your concern pertaining to your monetary claim. 1 crim case No. R-TAC-20-00537-CR; crim case No. R-TAC-20-00538-CR "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

We reiterate the applicable jurisprudence on the matter, to wit: As a matter of law, when a person indicted for an offense is arrested, he is deemed placed under the custody of the law. He is placed in actual restraint of liberty in jail so that he may be bound to answer for the commission of the offense. He must be detained in jail during the pendency of the case against him unless he is authorized by the court to be released on bail or on recognizance. Let it be stressed that all prisoners whether under preventive detention or serving final sentence cannot practice their profession nor engage in any business or occupation, or hold office, elective or appointive, while in detention. This is a necessary consequence of arrest and detention [emphasis supplied]2. In the light of recent pronouncements of the Supreme Court regarding the requirements necessary as to the entitlement of back salary, it held that: The rule on payment of back salaries during the period of suspension of a member of the civil service who is subsequently ordered reinstated, is already settled in this jurisdiction. Such payment of salaries corresponding to the period when an employee is not allowed to work may be decreed not only if he is found innocent of the charges which caused his suspension (Sec. 35, RA 2260), but also when the suspension is unjustified. xxx xxx xxx Bangalisan clearly laid down the principle that if the exoneration of the employee is relative (as distinguished from complete exoneration), an inquiry into the factual premise of the offense charged and of the offense committed must be made. If the administrative offense found to have been actually committed is of lesser gravity than the offense charged, the employee cannot be considered exonerated if the factual premise for the imposition of the lesser penalty remains the same. The employee found guilty of a lesser offense may only be entitled to back salaries when the offense actually committed does not carry the penalty of more than one month suspension or dismissal. Bangalisan reiterated that the payment of back salaries, during the period of suspension of a member of the civil service who is subsequently ordered reinstated, may be decreed only if the employee is found innocent of the charges which caused the suspension and when the suspension is unjustified. This pronouncement was re-echoed in Jacinto v. CA,5ß De la Cruz v. CA, and Hon. Gloria v. CA. xxx xxx xxx Thus, it is not enough that an employee is exonerated of the charqes against him. In addition, his suspension must be unjustified. The case of Bangalisan v. Court of Appeals itself similarly states that "payment of salaries corresponding to the period [1] when an employee is not allowed to work may be decreed if he is found innocent of the charges which caused his suspension and [2] when the suspension is unjustified." A careful reading of these cases would reveal that a strict observance of the second condition for an award of back salaries becomes important only if the employee is not totally innocent of any administrative infraction. As previously discussed, where the employee is completely exonerated of the administrative charge or acquitted in the criminal case arising from the same facts based on a finding of innocence, the second requirement becomes subsumed in the first. People v. Hon. Maceda, G.R. No. 89591-96; January 24, 2000. Page 2 of 3

Otherwise, a determination of the actis and offense/s actually committed and of the corresponding penalty imposed has to be made3. In applying the foregoing to the instant case, we take into consideration two (2) requisites. First is whether the sangguniang bayan member was found innocent of the charges which caused his suspension and/or inability to perform his functions. Second, is whether his suspension and/or inability to perform his functions was justified. Hence, as to the first requisite, the Judgment of the Regional Trial Court Branch 45 of Tacloban City acquitting you of the offense charged is present. However, as to the second requisite, we find that the suspension and/or inability to perform your functions was justified in view of your incarceration as to the offenses filed against you. Moreover, we take note that the court was constrained to acquit you not because of your innocence but because of the failure of the prosecution to prove your guilt beyond reasonable doubt. Premises considered, we are of the considered view that you are not entitled to your monetary claim during the period of your confinement despite the court finding you not guilty of the offense charged. Lastly, a person charged with a crime is taken into custody for purposes of the administration of justice. As stated in United States v. Gusti104, it is the injury to the public which State action in criminal law seeks to redress. It is not the injury to the complainant5. Further, the presumption of innocence does not carry with it the full enjoyment of civil and political rights6. Finally, this opinion is based solely on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. hope to have assisted you on this matter. JUA OR R.
